key_insight: With PRM scores fixed, product aggregation showed greater deletion-induced selection instability than geometric mean in all 14 evaluated checkpoint–benchmark cells.
engineering_relevance: Treat score aggregation as an independently auditable component of best-of-N reasoning selection, rather than attributing selector behavior solely to the PRM.
method: Freeze mathematical reasoning pools, scorer evidence, and deletion-intervention traces.
Compare product and geometric-mean reducers on recorded N=32 selection outcomes.
Reanalyze versioned outcomes with shared-problem bootstrap and a pre-defined sensitivity filter.
evidence_signal: Across seven checkpoints and two benchmarks, the equal-cell instability difference was +0.0965 (95% bootstrap interval: [0.0846, 0.1086]); filtering retained 4,459 of 4,622 records and yielded +0.0986.
watch_item: Missing primary edited-score vectors limit independent testing of new reducers; findings are conditional on the evaluated checkpoints and frozen pools, not deployment-wide evidence.
paper_title: StrictPRMBench: A Replayable Evaluation Benchmark for Auditing Fixed-Score PRM Aggregation
